record.paper_title: Some Recent Results and Open Problems on Sets of Lengths of Krull Monoids with Finite Class Group
record.context_brief: maximum distance in sets of lengths
record.original_question: Let G be a finite abelian group with |G| at least 3 and invariant-factor decomposition G ≅ C_{n1} ⊕ ... ⊕ C_{nr}, where C_n is a cyclic group of order n and 1 < n1 | ... | nr. For the monoid B(G) of zero-sum sequences over G, let Delta(G) denote the set of all positive gaps between consecutive lengths that occur in sets of factorization lengths of elements of B(G). Must the largest such distance satisfy max Delta(G) = max{nr - 2, -1 + sum_{i=1}^r floor(ni/2)}?

evidence.quote: Let A ⊂ Z. Then the set of distances of A, denoted by ∆(A), is the set of all differences between consecutive elements of A
Problem 5.7. Let G ∼= Cn1 ⊕ · · · ⊕ Cnr with |G| ≥ 3 and 1 < n1 | · · · | nr . Is max ∆(G) = max{nr − 2, −1 + sum floor(ni/2)}?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with $|G|\ge 3$, and let $G\cong C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_r}$ be its invariant-factor decomposition, where $C_n$ denotes the cyclic group of order $n$ and $1<n_1\mid n_2\mid\cdots\mid n_r$.

A sequence over $G$ is a finite unordered tuple $S=g_1\cdot\ldots\cdot g_\ell$ of elements of $G$ (repetitions allowed), and $S$ is called a zero-sum sequence if $g_1+\cdots+g_\ell=0$ in $G$. The set $\mathcal B(G)$ of all zero-sum sequences over $G$, with concatenation as operation, forms a commutative cancellative monoid (the monoid of zero-sum sequences). An element $U\in\mathcal B(G)$ is called an atom if it cannot be written as a product of two nontrivial zero-sum sequences. For a nonzero, non-unit $B\in\mathcal B(G)$, the set of (factorization) lengths is
$$\mathsf L(B)=\{k\in\mathbb N : B=U_1\cdot\ldots\cdot U_k\text{ with each }U_i\text{ an atom of }\mathcal B(G)\}.$$
For a finite set $L=\{m_1<m_2<\cdots<m_t\}\subset\mathbb Z$ of integers, define its set of distances $\Delta(L)=\{m_{i+1}-m_i : 1\le i<t\}$. Set
$$\Delta(G)=\bigcup_{B} \Delta(\mathsf L(B)),$$
the union taken over all $B\in\mathcal B(G)$ with $|\mathsf L(B)|\ge 2$.

Question: Does the equality
$$\max\Delta(G)\;=\;\max\!\Bigl\{\,n_r-2,\ -1+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Bigl\lfloor\frac{n_i}{2}\Bigr\rfloor\Bigr\}$$
hold for every such $G$?
artifact.category_tag: Sets of lengths in Krull monoids
artifact.status_search_result: A general closed-form formula for $\max\Delta(G)$ in terms of the invariant-factor decomposition does not appear to be established in the literature; the conjectured equality is stated as a problem and surveys on sets of lengths in Krull monoids over finite abelian groups continue to list the determination of $\max\Delta(G)$ as an open question, with results known only in special cases (cyclic groups, elementary $p$-groups, rank-two groups). No source confirming a proof of the stated equality for all finite abelian groups was found.

status_evidence.title: A realization theorem for sets of lengths in numerical monoids
status_evidence.snippet: Set of distances Δ(A) defined; invariants such as max Δ(G) for finite abelian groups are studied; explicit values known only in special cases.
status_evidence.claim: The exact value of max Δ(G) for general finite abelian groups is not given by a closed formula in the survey literature.

status_evidence.title: Sets of minimal distances and characterizations of class groups of Krull monoids
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Δ*(G) and Δ(G) for Krull monoids with finite class group G; determines these invariants only for restricted classes of groups.
status_evidence.claim: max Δ(G) is determined only in special cases, indicating the general formula remains conjectural.
